t: Section 4 of said Act (21 U.S.C. 72) is hereby amended by deleting the phrases “for human consumption” and “for transportation or sale”, and by inserting after the word “commerce” the phrase “which are capable of use as human food”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that deletes and inserts phrases in an existing statute to change the scope of products covered (those "capable of use as human food"). The only tempting reading is that it touches a regulatory inspection regime, but it creates no comment period, hearing, rulemaking authority, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely textual amendment to a statute, changing the definition of regulated items. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It simply alters the scope of the law's application.
qwen_block.s: Section 4 of said Act (21 U.S.C. 72) is hereby amended by deleting the phrases “for human consumption” and “for transportation or sale”, and by inserting after the word “commerce” the phrase “which are capable of use as human food”.

opus.w: This section only changes wording in 21 U.S.C. 72, which narrows or redefines the products it covers to those 'capable of use as human food.' It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The fact that the change may affect regulated companies does not mean those companies take part in any federal decision, so the 'Yes' reading fails.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** This section only changes wording in 21 U.S.C. 72, which appears to be part of the meat inspection laws. It deletes "for human consumption" and "for transportation or sale" and adds "which are capable of use as human food." The tempting reading is that changing the scope of a federal inspection law might affect outside parties like meat processors. That fails the definition, because nothing here involves an outside party in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely definitional amendment to a statute. It changes the legal definition of food but does not establish any process for consultation, comment, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in federal decision-making. It does not create an advisory board, require a public hearing, or grant rights to sue or object.
qwen_chat.s: Section 4 of said Act (21 U.S.C. 72) is hereby amended by deleting the phrases “for human consumption” and “for transportation or sale”, and by inserting after the word “commerce” the phrase “which are capable of use as human food”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the definition of "food" affects public health and thus implies public participation, or that the amendment process itself involves Congress (participation). However, the text is purely a definitional amendment to a statute. It does not establish a process for the public, states, or other outside entities to consult with the government, comment on rules, or participate in decision-making. It simply changes the legal scope of what constitutes food for regulatory purposes. There is no mechanism for outside involvement described in this section.
